newsitem.title: UK: Worldwide Advertising & Media Digest - July 3.
newsitem.headline: Worldwide Advertising & Media Digest - July 3.

text.p: ....REUTERS WORLDWIDE ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST.....
Reuters news from around the world on Advertising, Marketing, Media, the Internet, Brand-name Products and Consumer Trends
ADVERTISING & MARKETING:

LONDON - Despite the rise of increasingly sophisticated consumers around the world, the advertising industry finds the most basic humour its most effective tool in international ad campaigns. Toilet humour and slapstick are two of the easiest ways of communicating says an industry expert.
FRANKFURT - German sportswear maker Adidas, signs a multi-year global market alliance with the National Basketball Association, giving the company licensing rights to sell NBA merchandise in the U.S.

LONDON - London's annual Gay Pride Parade which takes place this weekend, will attract a number of corporate sponsors, including United Airlines, who recognise the power of the "pink pound". The UK gay market is worth six billion pounds ($10 billion) a year, says the Henley Centre for Forecasting.

WASHINGTON - The U.S. Federal Trade Commission and Canadian regulators launch a campaign to chip away at some $40 billion in annual investor losses caused by telemarketing scams. It is targeting telemarketing ploys used to lure investors into sham investments.
NEW YORK - TMP Worldwide Inc says it has bought three European recruitment advertising agencies in the Netherlands and Belgium.
PLYMOUTH, Wisconsin - Sargento Foods Inc. names DDB Needham Chicago as its ad agency following a multi-agency review that began in May.
MEDIA & THE INTERNET:

PARIS - The board of Canal Plus effectively decides to leave Europe's biggest television market, Germany, and strengthen the company's position in Italy. The company says it will sell its 37.5 percent stake in German pay-television company Premiere to the Kirch Gruppe.
BRUSSELS - The European Commission welcomes proposals by U.S. president Bill Clinton for a global internet free-trade zone, saying many of his suggestions mirror the EU's own initiatives.

LOS ANGELES - Time Warner Inc's Warner Bros. International Television says it has reached a pay television deal with Sogecable in Spain. Warner Bros. will provide Sogecable's Canal Satelite Digital and its premium pay television service Canal Plus Spain with pay television, pay-per-view and near video on demand feature films.

LONDON - British financial firms are still fairly new to the Internet according to a Reuters survey, but access is expected to rise, with 82 percent seeing the Internet becoming a significant business tool in five years.
BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS & MARKETS:

CHICAGO - Major U.S. cereal makers say they are taking a wait-and-see stance following a decision by General Mills Inc. earlier this week to increase cereal prices by an average of 2.6 percent. *********
PARIS - LVMH chairman Bernard Arnault has proposed a merger of LVMH's wine and spirits business with those of Guinness and Grand Metropolitan in a quoted company, LVMH says.
LONDON - Shares in British household products group Reckitt and Colman Plc score record highs on rumours of a take-over bid by Unilever Plc, traders say.
PARIS - The number of mobile phone users in France grew by 6.3 percent in May to 3.27 million, the telecommunications authority ART says.
TURIN - Alfa Romeo, Italy's famous sporty car company has remained in the doldrums for decades but the company says this is set to change with the launch this autumn of a sporty executive car.
CONSUMER TRENDS:

CAIRO - Egyptian drinkers are looking forward to the arrival of international brewing giants such as Danish firm Carlsberg onto the Egyptian market, say industry observers. The company has signed a deal to build and operate a $50 million brewery, which will begin producing Carlsberg's "Green Label" beer in Egypt by 1999.

SHANGHAI - China's life insurance market is expanding fast, especially in the booming east coast city of Shanghai, due to cutbacks in the social welfare system and rising incomes, industry analysts say.

LONDON - It might just be the perfect accessory for that up-and-comer who has everything -- an aristocratic title with a thousand-year history. Consumers flock to an auction of manorial titles in London spending a total of nearly 400,000 pounds ($663,000)in order to call themselves lords and ladies.
SYDNEY - Consumers are demanding a better deal on credit cards, with most opting for annual upfront fees instead of individual transaction charges, according to a new survey.
